summary: zero-baileys 3.3.5: WhatsApp library fork with unverified static pattern match
details: zero-baileys is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library. A a static rule matched on lib/Utils/messages-media.js due to co-occurrence of require('child_process'), https.request(), and POST tokens in the same file. This is the expected shape of a WhatsApp media-handling module, which legitimately performs HTTPS requests to WhatsApp/Meta media endpoints and may spawn ffmpeg/child processes for media transcoding. No specific installer-side data read is traced to a non-first-party destination, no lifecycle scripts are shown to auto-execute the flagged code path, and no hardcoded attacker domain is named in the evidence. Baileys forks published under alternate names have historically included covert side-effects such as auto-following/subscribing to author-controlled channels using the installer's session; that risk is not confirmed here from the available evidence but is a known pattern for this package family.
